CatalogFacets.description:
Distinct filter values for the Explorer's chain / category selectors.

Sourced from the stored catalog rather than a hardcoded list, so the options
track what was actually discovered.
CatalogFacets.title: CatalogFacets

CatalogPageSize.description:
Closed set of page sizes the catalog Explorer may request.

An ``IntEnum`` rather than ``Literal[25, 50, 100]`` on purpose: FastAPI binds
query parameters as *strings*, and Pydantic coerces a numeric string into an
int enum but refuses to coerce it into an integer ``Literal`` - so the latter
would reject every legitimate ``?page_size=25`` request with a 422. Enumerating
here still emits the closed ``[25, 50, 100]`` set in the OpenAPI schema.
CatalogPageSize.title: CatalogPageSize

CatalogSyncStats.description:
Outcome of one catalog synchronization, returned by the sync endpoint.

Every counter is reported rather than hidden behind a bare "ok": an operator
needs to see how many rows were inserted vs updated vs left alone, and which
malformed entries were skipped, to trust that a sync did not lose data.
CatalogSyncStats.title: CatalogSyncStats

ChatCitation.description:
A numbered source an answer is grounded in. ``n`` matches the [n] marker
inline in the answer text; ``quote`` is the exact passage retrieved.
ChatCitation.title: ChatCitation

CoverageStatus.description:
Public, aggregate view of what the service has actually observed.

Every count is nullable, and the null is load-bearing: ``null`` means
"could not be measured" (the store was unreachable, or a probe failed)
while ``0`` means "measured, and there are none". A landing page that
renders this must show the difference - reporting zero for an unreachable
database would be the exact lie the rest of the product is built to avoid.

No row-level data and no secrets are exposed here: configuration flags are
reported as booleans (``llm_configured``), never as values.
CoverageStatus.title: CoverageStatus

DashboardResponse.description:
Everything the dashboard needs, sourced from the DB (latest snapshot
per protocol + alert_records) with a live DefiLlama hydration fallback.

``withheld_alerts`` is the number of critical alerts the caller's clearance
was not sufficient to read. It is reported rather than hidden: a board that
silently shows three fewer alerts than exist would be lying by omission.
DashboardResponse.title: DashboardResponse

Mover.description: A protocol ranked by 7d TVL change (used for top gainers/losers).
Mover.title: Mover

OnchainActivityOut.description:
On-chain activity from Dune - the second, additive data provider.

Always present on a research payload, because *why* there is no number is
part of the answer: ``unconfigured`` (no key), ``no_data`` (no curated
mapping or nothing captured yet), ``stale``, ``partial`` (a mapped chain
did not report) or ``ok``. An omitted block could not tell those apart, and
a zero would assert "no activity" - a claim these measurements never make.

``source`` is per block rather than per protocol: this block is Dune's,
while ``ProtocolOverview.source`` stays DefiLlama's.
OnchainActivityOut.title: OnchainActivityOut

ProtocolCatalogItem.description:
One row of the discovery catalog, as the Explorer lists it.

Deliberately *not* ``ProtocolOverview``: the catalog spans thousands of
protocols of which only a handful are monitored, so it carries the identity
and market-metadata DefiLlama supplies for everyone, plus the risk fields
only a scored protocol has. Missing metrics stay ``None`` (a gap), never 0.
ProtocolCatalogItem.title: ProtocolCatalogItem

ProtocolCatalogPage.description:
A single page of the catalog plus the metadata the Explorer needs.

``total`` is the count of rows matching the active filters (before paging),
``pages`` the derived page count - both computed server-side so the UI never
loads the whole catalog to paginate locally.
ProtocolCatalogPage.title: ProtocolCatalogPage

RiskAssessmentOut.description:
Typed shape of ``scoring.RiskAssessment.to_dict()``. Declaring it here
(rather than a bare ``dict``) makes the explainable-risk structure part of
the OpenAPI contract so the frontend's generated types stay precise.
RiskAssessmentOut.title: RiskAssessmentOut

RiskPoint.description:
One daily risk-score observation from ``protocol_snapshots``.

Only rows the scheduler actually scored carry a ``score``/``band``; the
deep DefiLlama backfill seeds TVL history without re-scoring every day, so
those are excluded from the trend rather than plotted as zero.
RiskPoint.title: RiskPoint

SubjectOut.description:
The authenticated caller, as the UI needs it.

``categories`` / ``chains`` come back as ``["*"]`` when the axis is
unrestricted, and ``permissions`` is the resolved RBAC verb list so the
client can disable a control instead of discovering the 403 the hard way.
SubjectOut.title: SubjectOut

SwitchRequest.description: Demo-mode role switch: re-issue a session for another seeded account.
SwitchRequest.title: SwitchRequest

TicketResponse.description: Single-use credential for the browser-opened ``WS /ws/chat`` socket.
TicketResponse.title: TicketResponse

info.description: DeFi protocol research, explainable risk scoring and monitoring API
info.title: DeFiScope AI

get.description:
Today's active alerts, served straight from the durable log.

This is a fast DB read - it does NOT trigger a crawl. The scheduler and
``POST /api/alerts/run`` are the owners of the (expensive) DefiLlama
monitoring pass that populates these rows.

Critical alerts above the caller's clearance are withheld from the body and
counted in ``X-Withheld-Alerts``: the reader still learns that something
broke, without learning what.

schema.title: Response Current Alerts Api Alerts Get
Response Alert History Api Alerts History Get

post.description:
Manual trigger for a full monitoring pass: crawl the watchlist,
evaluate rules, persist alerts + daily snapshots, then return the alerts
that fired on this pass (the same set ``GET /api/alerts`` will now serve).

Gated twice beyond the role: a pass outside business hours is refused, and a
pass over a *fresh* snapshot is refused as redundant - a crawl that cannot
change anything is wasted upstream quota, not diligence. Both denials come
back as an explanation rather than a bare 403.

schema.title: Response Run Alert Check Api Alerts Run Post

post.description:
Delete the session row. Idempotent: an already-dead token is not an error,
because the caller's intent (be logged out) is satisfied either way.

Demo only: become another seeded account without typing a password.

Disabled in ``required`` mode - impersonation is a tour affordance, not a
feature of a real deployment. The caller's previous session is revoked so
the switch is an identity transition rather than a second live credential.

Mint a single-use, short-lived credential for the browser's WebSocket.

Gated on ``chat:ask`` so the ticket can never out-rank the verb that
matters: a role that cannot ask questions cannot get a socket either.

get.description:
Render the brief for download as Markdown, CSV or PDF.

Returns raw bytes with a ``Content-Disposition: attachment`` header so the
browser saves the file. Unknown formats are a 400; an unfetchable protocol
is a 404 (mirrors the JSON brief endpoint). The web app proxies this through
a same-origin route handler so the compose-internal API URL stays server-side.

The confidence gate is evaluated after the brief is composed because
confidence is a property of the brief itself - there is no cheaper way to
know it in advance. A denied export therefore costs the same generation as
an allowed one; the cost ceiling for that lives in the deferred
per-subject rate limiting, not here.

post.description:
Idempotently upsert the full DefiLlama directory into the catalog.

Returns per-outcome counters (inserted / updated / unchanged / skipped /
duplicates) so an operator can see the sync did not lose or duplicate rows.
Re-running it is safe: existing rows are updated in place and rows the
provider no longer lists are left untouched.

get.description:
Latest snapshot per protocol + aggregate stats + alert feed, all read
from the DB. Hydrates from DefiLlama only when the DB is empty/stale.

Paginated protocol discovery catalog, served entirely from the DB.

Pagination, search, filtering and sorting all happen server-side; only one
page of rows is ever returned. ``sort`` is bound to an allowlisted column
(see ``catalog.SORT_COLUMNS``) - the caller's string never reaches SQL as
text - and ordering is made deterministic with a slug tiebreak.

Distinct chain and category values present in the catalog, for the
Explorer's filter selectors. Declared before ``/{slug}`` so "facets" is not
swallowed as a protocol slug.

schema.title: Response Protocol History Api Protocols  Slug  History Get

get.description:
Daily composite risk-score trend for one protocol (DB read, no crawl).

Only days the scheduler actually scored are returned, so the series reflects
real observed risk rather than the null-scored DefiLlama backfill rows.

schema.title: Response Protocol Risk History Api Protocols  Slug  Risk History Get

get.description: Aggregate coverage of the store: protocols, days, bands, alerts, index.
